datasets.dataset_title: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 Public — bounded western Pyrenean and Beaujolais tile sets

derived_artifacts.role: Terrain descriptor: bounded extents, placement, intervals and attribution for the Atlas

geographic_extent.description: Outer envelope of two discontinuous pinned tile groups. CARTA has terrain only in the named western-Pyrenean and Beaujolais regions below; the intervening envelope has no acquired coverage and no France-wide elevation ingestion exists.

regions.description: Six pinned 1°×1° tiles covering the western Pyrenees, the Béarn foothills and the Adour basin.
Two pinned 1°×1° tiles covering the bounded Beaujolais proof and ordinary surrounding terrain context.

datasets.geographic_meaning: Digital surface model in two bounded terrain proofs: bare ground plus vegetation canopy and buildings as observed by TanDEM-X between 2011 and 2015. It is physical relief context for CARTA Atlas. It is not evidence about vineyard land, planted parcels, growing conditions, ripening, drainage, climate or wine quality.

measurement.native_resolution: 1 arc-second grid (3600×3600 samples per 1° tile); ≈30 m north–south and ≈21–23 m east–west across the acquired 42–47°N coverage
measurement.scale_limitations: Usable for regional relief reading down to roughly 1:50,000. It cannot resolve an individual vineyard parcel, a terrace, a wall or a row orientation, and as a surface model it carries tree canopy and building heights as if they were ground.
measurement.uncertainty: The programme specification is LE90 < 4 m vertical and CE90 < 6 m horizontal. The six western-Pyrenean source entries retain their separately checked tile-mask figures; no tile-mask precision beyond the programme specification is asserted for the two Beaujolais files.

datasets.publisher: Copernicus programme — European Union and ESA (data © DLR e.V. and Airbus Defence and Space GmbH)
datasets.refresh_policy: Pinned snapshot. CARTA re-acquires only when a Copernicus DEM release changes one of the eight governed files, or when an approved proof needs a bounded extent these two tile groups do not cover. Terrain is context, not a live feed, so there is no scheduled refresh.

datasets.geographic_meaning: Ordinary geographic presentation context including countries, cities, roads, rivers, coasts, borders, and physical labels; not CARTA wine-domain authority

semantic_distinctions: Wine-region labels are derived CARTA orientation points, not statutory polygons.
INAO areas are cartographic representations of regulatory geographical areas, not parcel eligibility or actual vineyard land.
Eligible communes, approved viticultural parcels, actual vineyard land, cadastral parcels, and lieux-dits remain distinct concepts.
External sourced geography may be displayed without becoming a native CARTA guide or subject.
Terrain is context before it is interpretation: relief, slope or elevation shown on the map never authorises a claim about grape growing, ripening, drainage, climate or wine quality.
